title: [BUG] Custom slash commands can't request the user's permission to execute bash scripts
body:
## Environment
- Platform (select one):
  - [ ] Anthropic API
  - [ ] AWS Bedrock
  - [ ] Google Vertex AI
  - [x] Other: Claude Code on macOS
- Claude CLI version: 1.0.52
- Operating System: macOS 15.5
- Terminal:  iTerm2

## Bug Description

Following your documentation, I've attempted to set up three custom slash commands, each of which is supposed to invoke a different tiny shell script to respectively **enable**, **disable**, and **report status** on Pushover notifications sent to my iPhone by a custom hook script.

I can run the shell scripts from the command line just fine, and Claude Code has been able to execute them via prompt (after tokenizing the request and processing for several seconds), but I can't make the slash commands run them as they're supposed to.

The three commands are in a directory named `phone` inside the ~/.claude/commands/ directory.

Here are the contents of the three custom slash command Markdown files:

**off.md**
```markdown
---
description: Disable Claude Code phone notifications
---

!`~/.claude/bin/claude-phone-off`
```
**on.md**
```markdown
---
description: Enable Claude Code phone notifications
---

!`~/.claude/bin/claude-phone-on`
```
**status.md**
```markdown
---
description: Check Claude Code phone notification status
---

!`./claude-phone-status`
```

I'm supposed to be able to invoke them via `/phone:on`, `/phone:off`, and `/phone:status`, but when I try, Claude either doesn't see that they're slash commands at all (begins looking in the codebase for phone-related code, or can't get my permission to run a bash command outside the `cwd`.

## Additional Context

**Conversation between me and the model about the commands:**

⏺ I can see that the /phone:off command is also being recognized and attempting to run. This confirms that your custom slash commands are set up correctly:

  - /phone:status - Check notification status
  - /phone:on - Enable notifications
  - /phone:off - Disable notifications

  The issue is that these commands need Bash permissions to execute the scripts in ~/.claude/bin/. When you run a custom slash command that uses the ! syntax to execute shell commands,
  Claude Code needs permission to run those commands.

  Your custom slash command implementation is working perfectly. The earlier confusion where I searched the codebase instead of recognizing /phone:status as a custom command appears to
  be a bug in how I initially respond to custom commands in new sessions.

  To use these commands, you'll need to grant Bash permissions when prompted, allowing the underlying scripts to run and manage the notification state by creating or removing the
  ~/.claude/notifications-disabled file.

> But I'm not being prompted.

⏺ You're right - that's the bug! When a custom slash command runs, you should be getting a prompt to grant Bash permissions, but instead you're just seeing an error message saying "you
  haven't granted it yet" without actually being prompted.

  This appears to be a bug in Claude Code where:
  1. Custom slash commands are recognized (good)
  2. They attempt to execute shell commands (good)
  3. But the permission prompt isn't being shown to you (bug)

  So you're stuck - the command needs Bash permission to run, but you're not being given the opportunity to grant it.

  This is definitely something that should be reported as a bug. You could file an issue at https://github.com/anthropics/claude-code/issues describing:
  - Custom slash commands that execute shell scripts don't prompt for Bash permissions
  - Instead, they show an error saying permissions haven't been granted
  - There's no way to actually grant the permissions

  As a workaround, you might be able to:
  1. Run a regular Bash command first (like ls) to get the permission prompt
  2. Then try your custom slash command again

  But this is clearly a bug in the permission flow for custom slash commands.

! ls ~/.claude/commands/
  ⎿  phone
